title: Course, position & traffic
goal: Report other ships as lookout: what, where, how far, and the bearing.

l17-01.text: Busy afternoon, Diego. This is the Florida Strait. Report every ship you see.
l17-01.es: Tarde movida, Diego. Este es el Estrecho de Florida. Reportá cada buque que veas.

l17-05.text: Good. Now take a bearing, and again in three minutes.
l17-05.es: Bien. Ahora tomá una marcación, y otra en tres minutos.

l17-06.text: Bearing zero four five… Now zero four five again. The bearing is steady.
l17-06.es: Marcación cero cuatro cinco… Ahora cero cuatro cinco otra vez. La marcación se mantiene.

l17-07.text: Steady bearing, and the range is closing. What does that mean?
l17-07.es: Marcación constante, y la distancia se achica. ¿Qué significa eso?

l17-09.text: Exactly. She's crossing from starboard, so we give way. I'm altering course to starboard.
l17-09.es: Exacto. Nos cruza desde estribor, así que maniobramos nosotros. Caigo a estribor.

l17-10.text: Another ship on the port quarter. She's overtaking us.
l17-10.es: Otro buque por la aleta de babor. Nos está alcanzando.

l17-11.text: Overtaking. She keeps clear of us. Good report.
l17-11.es: Alcanzando. Ella se mantiene apartada. Buen reporte.

l17-12.text: And one ship right ahead. Head-on!
l17-12.es: Y un buque justo adelante. ¡De vuelta encontrada!

l17-13.text: Head-on: both ships alter to starboard. Let's check the CPA on the radar… One point five miles. Watch her.
l17-13.es: De vuelta encontrada: los dos caen a estribor. Veamos el CPA en el radar… Una coma cinco millas. Vigilalo.

l17-15.text: Three ships under two miles. Captain's orders: we call him. Diego, call the Captain to the bridge.
l17-15.es: Tres buques a menos de dos millas. Órdenes del Capitán: lo llamamos. Diego, llamá al Capitán al puente.

l17-16.text: Yes, Chief. Calling the Captain now.
l17-16.es: Sí, jefa. Llamo al Capitán ahora.

screens.title: What, where, how far
steps: on the starboard bow · on the port beam · on the port quarter · right ahead · astern
paras: Always in this order: what, where, how far. Short, no verb needed.
bow = between ahead and the beam · beam = at 90° · quarter = between the beam and astern. Plus port or starboard.
screens.avoid: There is a ship that is coming from the right. · Ship in the starboard bow.

screens.situation: A ship ahead and a little to the left, 4 miles.
screens.q: Report it.
Write the bearing, three digits.

screens.title: Bearing is not course
paras: course = rumbo: where our ship goes. bearing = marcación: the direction from us to another ship or object.
And range is distancia, not rango. Use on the bow, not in.
screens.avoid: The course of the other ship is zero four five (when you mean bearing). · in the starboard bow

screens.q: The bearing is changing. Is there a risk of collision?
screens.why: A steady bearing with a closing range is the danger. A changing bearing usually means she passes clear.

screens.title: Quarter, CPA
paras: CPA: three letters, see-pee-AY, stress on the last one. Remember the letters from Lesson 5.
